one_line_contribution: That contamination in a shared experience bank is governed by writer-reader policy proximity rather than by writer capability or item content: relabelled failures written by the reader's own policy both harm the reader most and are the items the reader's own read-time judgment is least able to reject, with a foreign-backbone judge recovering the harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
closest_prior_work: Verified: arXiv:2606.24428, 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning' (2026-06-23, S2, 1 citation) — it already names the self-confirmation trap in agentic experience learning and already fixes it with multiple *heterogeneous* agents verifying experiences before they enter the store. That is the proposal's P5 mechanism (a foreign judge filters what the writer's own judgment endorses), demonstrated end-to-end and shown to beat baselines. It does not manipulate writer identity as an independent variable, does not report per-writer detection precision/recall in a judge x writer table, and does not measure downstream harm as a function of measured policy proximity, so it does not scoop the interaction claim; but it does mean the proposal's practical payload ('use a different backbone to filter the bank') is already published advice, and a reviewer will read P5 as confirmation rather than discovery. Second threat, and the one the proposal never cites: the self-correction blind spot line — arXiv:2507.02778 Self-Correction Bench (verified, 16 citations: LLMs reliably fix an identical error attributed to an external source and fail to fix it in their own output, established by controlled error injection) and arXiv:2607.09803 (verified, 2026-07-09, a formal account of the same effect). P3 and P4 are that phenomenon re-measured on ALFWorld trajectories; the proposal's contribution there is the agentic instantiation, not the effect. Third: arXiv:2410.21819 Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge (verified, 286 citations) shows judge leniency tracks familiarity/perplexity of the text, and arXiv:2608.18091 (verified) shows authorship labels alone drive bidirectional judge bias — these are not just prior work, they are the confound in P3 (see strongest objection). The Compliance Trap arXiv:2607.10608 (verified) and MemoryGraft arXiv:2512.16962 (verified, 59 citations) are correctly positioned and do not threaten the claim.
strongest_objection: The detection half of the title ('least able to detect') is confounded with ordinary self-preference, and the design as written cannot separate them. Each judge's operating point is calibrated to a 5 percent false-rejection rate on *clean expert items only* — a single, writer-agnostic threshold — and the diagonal deficit is then read off recall in the judge x writer table. But a judge that is uniformly more lenient toward its own backbone's prose (documented, familiarity/perplexity-driven, 2410.21819; authorship-label-driven, 2608.18091) produces exactly a diagonal recall deficit at a threshold calibrated on someone else's text, with no failure-detection blind spot required. The pre-registered covariate (each judge's overall recall) removes a judge main effect, not self-text leniency, so it does not fix this. The proposal collects 600 clean self items for Q only, so it cannot even estimate the per-column self-preference offset for E or G. P4 is offered as the rescue, but the entailment check is right that its L1 falsifier is nearly unreachable (it demands CI upper bounds below 0.05 for *both* judges against a ~0.063 paired half-width, i.e. point estimates below -0.013 twice over), so the arm that is supposed to show the deficit is about judging actions rather than trusting an appended label will in practice return 'underpowered' rather than adjudicate. Second blade: the one arm that converts P1 from 'Q's failed text hurts Q' into a proximity claim — the reader-E mirror, D_E — is the least powered cell in the design (6 vs 6 seeds, half-width 4.6) and sits on a reader whose clean gain is itself unmeasured and may be small. If D_E lands inconclusive, the headline reduces to a single-reader observation compatible with 'Q-self failures are simply worse text', and the proposal's own risk section concedes the mirror is a sign test, not a margin test.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Calibrate the 5 percent false-rejection point per judge *per writer column* on that writer's own clean successes — which requires collecting clean success items for E and G, not only Q — or subtract the measured clean-item self-preference gap from each deficit and pre-register the adjusted deficit as the estimand. Without this the deficit measures style familiarity and P3 is near-entailed. (2) Restate P4's L1 clause as a single-deficit inferiority test (CI excluding 0.08, or the L0-minus-L1 drop CI excluding zero) and raise per-writer item counts from 600 toward 2,000; item-level judgments are cheap relative to the 28k episodes. (3) Run the filter cells on the E-self bank as well as the Q-self bank (Q-filters-E and E-filters-E), so P5 tests the diagonal at the harm level instead of comparing two judges on one bank; add a removal-rate-matched random-deletion control so 'foreign filter is better' cannot be 'foreign filter removed more items'. (4) Express R(cross) as a fraction of realised harm(Q-self) rather than a fixed 6 net, since at the Gate-0 floor of 6 the stated margin demands near-total recovery. (5) Raise the reader-E mirror to at least 8 seeds and pre-register a minimum clean gain for reader E, since the mirror is what makes this a proximity paper. (6) Cite and position against the self-correction blind spot literature explicitly — a reviewer who knows 2507.02778 will otherwise read P3/P4 as a port.
missing_baseline: Filter cells on the foreign writer's bank. P5 runs own-judgment vs cross-judge filters on the Q-self bank only, so 'the foreign judge recovers harm the own judge cannot' is indistinguishable from 'EXAONE is simply a better trajectory judge on this item distribution' — the covariate adjustment that guards against this in the offline recall table has no counterpart in the downstream harm cells. The discriminating arms are Q-filters-the-E-self-bank and E-filters-the-E-self-bank at the same matched false-rejection point: proximity predicts a crossover, better-judge predicts E wins in both banks. Two 8-seed cells (~4,400 episodes) buy the entire causal claim of P5 and are omitted. Secondary omission: a removal-rate-matched random-deletion filter, without which any filter advantage is partly a bank-size effect.
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim; the proposal's own check is above average for this pipeline but searched the wrong home literature and missed the two nearest recent preprints. Queries I ran, all through the literature command (s2cli.py, S2 + HF both 'ok'; WebSearch unavailable per session rules, WebFetch never used): (a) 'self-preference LLM judge cannot detect its own generated errors blind spot' --recent -> 2607.09803 (spectral account of the self-correction blind spot), 2507.02778 (Self-Correction Bench, 16 cit), 2410.21819 (Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge, 286 cit), plus judge-bias auditing (2604.16790, 2602.09383); (b) 'agent experience memory contaminated by writer identity self-written failed trajectories harm reader' --recent -> 2606.24428 (EDV, self-confirmation trap, heterogeneous verifiers), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2605.29463 (Honest Lying: self-generated reflections stored as confident but wrong), 2605.12978 (LLM-consolidated memory degrades, raw trajectories better), 2512.16962 (MemoryGraft), 2607.06595, 2510.02373; (c) 'self-confirmation trap heterogeneous verifier agent experience self-generated errors cross-model verification' -> 2606.24428 again, 2605.02915 (when should a model trust its own self-verification), 2603.17775 (consensus trap, generator-verifier co-evolution); (d) 'models detect errors in other models outputs better than their own cross-model critique asymmetry' --recent -> nothing closer (2604.22271, 2603.16331); (e) 'in-context demonstrations from the model's own policy versus another model suboptimal demonstrations negative transfer imitation' -> 2606.05588 (action-only curation metrics miss structural defects; relevant to the filter arm, uncited); (f) 'filtering experience bank with a different backbone judge...' --recent -> nothing closer (2603.04549 admission control, 2505.15143 filtering learning histories). COULD NOT VERIFY: arXiv:2608.10509, cited in Related Work as 'provenance gating' — not found on S2 or HF; the proposal should drop or correct it. Judgment on the proposal's check: it names its channel, its queries, its retry strategy and its IDs, and it verifies its closest named result by ID, which is what the round asks for. But its 'home vocabulary' search went to semi-supervised pseudo-labeling, a distant analogy, and therefore missed the actual home literature of its own mechanism — the LLM self-correction blind spot, where the effect it predicts in P3/P4 has already been established by controlled error injection (2507.02778), and LLM-judge self-preference, which is simultaneously the nearest prior result and the confound in its measurement (2410.21819, 2608.18091). It also missed 2606.24428, published two months before the check was run, which names the self-confirmation trap in agentic experience learning and already deploys the heterogeneous-verifier remedy that P5 proposes to discover. None of these manipulates writer identity in a shared experience bank, measures per-writer downstream harm, or supplies the reader-swap reversal, so novelty is not capped — but it is reduced from 'new mechanism' to 'new interaction of two documented mechanisms', and the check as submitted overstates how clear the field is.
